description: email.rs: validate_and_normalize_keywords(raw: HashMap<String, bool>) takes the raw keyword map by value (move). The caller at line 1413 constructs it from serde_json::from_value and immediately passes it, so the move is free there. However the function signature signals 'I consume and return a new map' when a &HashMap parameter with an owned return would express the same intent with less API surface pressure. More importantly: the function iterates the raw map and builds a new result: HashMap<Keyword, bool> — this is a collect() from an iterator, not a loop-with-push pattern. The idiomatic form is: raw.into_iter().filter(|(_, v)| *v).try_fold(HashMap::new(), |mut acc, (kw, _)| { validate_kw(&kw)?; acc.insert(Keyword::from(kw.to_ascii_lowercase()), true); Ok(acc) }) or equivalently .map(...).collect::<Result<HashMap<_,_>, _>>() which expresses the validation-and-collect in one pass.
title: validate_and_normalize_keywords takes HashMap by value — callers must move or clone
